indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.1.1.1 Show understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicator.objective: Classify plants based on their root system

skills.description: Name the two main root systems: tap root and fibrous root.
Describe a tap root as one main root with smaller side roots (e.g. mango, cassava, bean).
Describe a fibrous root as many thin roots of similar size spreading out (e.g. grass, maize, rice).
Classify named plants into tap root or fibrous root groups.
Give a simple reason for classifying a plant into a root group based on observable features.
Compare the differences between tap roots and fibrous roots.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: All plants have the same root system.
Tap roots are always bigger than the whole plant.
Fibrous roots are just broken tap roots.
You cannot classify plants by their roots.

questions.stem: Which two main root systems are used to classify plants?
hints: One has a single main root.
The other has many thin roots.
questions.explanation: Plants are classified by their root systems into tap roots and fibrous roots.
questions.misconception: All plants have the same root system.

questions.stem: What is a tap root system?
options: One main root with smaller side roots
Many thin roots of the same size
Roots that grow above the ground
Roots that only grow in water
hints: Think about a carrot or a mango seedling.
It has one thick main root.
questions.explanation: A tap root system has one main root with smaller side roots growing from it.
questions.misconception: Tap roots have many equal-sized roots.

questions.stem: Name the two main types of root systems.
hints: One is thick and single.
The other is many thin roots.
questions.explanation: The two main root systems are tap root and fibrous root.
questions.misconception: Plants only have one type of root.

questions.stem: Which of these plants has a tap root?
hints: Which one has one main root?
Grass and maize have many thin roots.
questions.explanation: A mango plant has a tap root — one main root with smaller side roots.
questions.misconception: Mango has a fibrous root.

questions.stem: Which description best fits a tap root?
options: Many thin roots of similar size spreading out
One thick main root with smaller side roots
Roots that grow from the leaves
hints: Tap roots have one main root.
Side roots grow from it.
questions.explanation: A tap root is one thick main root with smaller side roots growing from it.
questions.misconception: Tap roots are many thin roots.

questions.stem: Describe a tap root system.
answer: one main root with smaller side roots
one thick main root and smaller side roots
a single main root with side roots
hints: Think about one main root.
Smaller roots branch off it.
questions.explanation: A tap root system has one main root with smaller side roots growing from it.
questions.misconception: Tap roots are many thin roots.

questions.stem: A pupil uproots a bean plant and sees one main root with smaller roots branching from it. What type of root system is this?
hints: There is one main root.
Smaller roots branch from it.
questions.explanation: The bean plant has a tap root system — one main root with smaller side roots.
questions.misconception: Beans have fibrous roots.

questions.stem: Which of these plants has a fibrous root?
hints: Which one has many thin roots?
Mango and cassava have one main root.
questions.explanation: Grass has a fibrous root system — many thin roots of similar size spreading out.
questions.misconception: Grass has a tap root.

questions.stem: Which description best fits a fibrous root?
options: One thick main root with side roots
Many thin roots of similar size spreading out
Roots that do not absorb water
hints: Fibrous roots are many and thin.
They are all about the same size.
questions.explanation: A fibrous root system has many thin roots of similar size spreading out from the base of the stem.
questions.misconception: Fibrous roots are one main root.

questions.stem: Describe a fibrous root system.
answer: many thin roots of similar size spreading out
many thin roots of the same size
many fine roots spreading out from the stem
hints: Think about many thin roots.
They are all about the same size.
questions.explanation: A fibrous root system has many thin roots of similar size spreading out from the base of the stem.
questions.misconception: Fibrous roots are one main root.

questions.stem: A pupil uproots a maize plant and sees many thin roots of the same size. What type of root system is this?
hints: There are many thin roots.
They are all the same size.
questions.explanation: The maize plant has a fibrous root system — many thin roots of similar size.
questions.misconception: Maize has a tap root.

questions.stem: Which group correctly lists plants with tap roots?
hints: Which plants have one main root?
Mango, cassava and bean all have one main root.
questions.explanation: Mango, cassava and bean have tap roots.
questions.misconception: Cassava has a fibrous root.

questions.stem: Which group correctly lists plants with fibrous roots?
hints: Which plants have many thin roots?
Grass, maize and rice all have many thin roots.
questions.explanation: Grass, maize and rice have fibrous roots.
questions.misconception: Maize has a tap root.

questions.stem: Classify these plants into tap roots and fibrous roots: mango, grass, cassava, maize.
answer: tap roots: mango, cassava; fibrous roots: grass, maize
mango and cassava are tap roots; grass and maize are fibrous roots
tap: mango, cassava; fibrous: grass, maize
hints: Which have one main root?
Which have many thin roots?
questions.explanation: Mango and cassava have tap roots. Grass and maize have fibrous roots.
questions.misconception: All plants have the same root type.

questions.stem: A pupil classifies a plant as having a fibrous root because it has many thin roots. Which plant could it be?
hints: Which plant has many thin roots?
Rice has a fibrous root system.
questions.explanation: Rice has many thin roots of similar size, so it has a fibrous root system.
questions.misconception: Rice has a tap root.

questions.stem: Why is a cassava plant classified as having a tap root?
options: It has one main root with smaller side roots
It has roots that grow above the ground
hints: Cassava has one main root.
Smaller roots branch from it.
questions.explanation: Cassava is classified as having a tap root because it has one main root with smaller side roots.
questions.misconception: Cassava has a fibrous root.

questions.stem: Give one reason why a maize plant is classified as having a fibrous root.
answer: it has many thin roots of similar size
it has many thin roots spreading out
it has many fine roots of the same size
hints: Think about the number of roots.
They are all thin and similar.
questions.explanation: Maize is classified as having a fibrous root because it has many thin roots of similar size spreading out from the base of the stem.
questions.misconception: Maize has a tap root.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'A plant with a tap root must be bigger than a plant with a fibrous root.' Is the pupil correct?
options: Yes, tap root plants are always bigger
No, root type does not determine plant size
Yes, fibrous root plants are always smaller
No, only the roots are different
hints: Can a small plant have a tap root?
Root type and plant size are not the same.
questions.explanation: No, root type does not determine plant size. Small plants can have tap roots, and large plants can have fibrous roots.
questions.misconception: Tap roots are always bigger than the whole plant.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares tap roots and fibrous roots?
options: Tap roots have one main root; fibrous roots have many thin roots of similar size
Tap roots have many thin roots; fibrous roots have one main root
hints: One has a single main root.
The other has many equal-sized roots.
questions.explanation: Tap roots have one main root with smaller side roots, while fibrous roots have many thin roots of similar size.
questions.misconception: Tap roots and fibrous roots are the same.

questions.stem: Explain one difference between a tap root and a fibrous root.
answer: a tap root has one main root with side roots, while a fibrous root has many thin roots of similar size
tap root: one main root; fibrous root: many thin roots of the same size
tap roots have one main root, fibrous roots have many equal-sized roots
hints: Think about the number of main roots.
One has one main root; the other has many.
questions.explanation: A tap root has one main root with smaller side roots, while a fibrous root has many thin roots of similar size.
questions.misconception: Tap roots and fibrous roots are the same.
